messages:
Samir: Quick sync 1 PRs conflict on parse fallback for tool-calling examples. One uses an `envelope` always, the other uses compact JSON when parse succeeds. Which do we standardize?
Maria Chen: I prefer compact in the tutorial, but must include a migration note for SDKs still expecting envelopes.
Jake L: Agree. Tutorial -> compact. Put envelope pattern in an advanced/compatibility section. Many customers rely on it.
Olivia P: Plan: tutorial + compact snippets; separate "interop" section showing envelope fallback and handler pseudo-code. I'll fix broken links to archived "invoke" page while at it.
Samir: Proposed pseudo: `if parse_success: return parsed_obj else: return {"tool_name": t, "raw": raw_string}`. Keep `raw` as string in examples to avoid nested assumptions.
Maria Chen: I'll author a Python snippet that handles both shapes and add a unit-test example: `assert parse(e) or fallback(e)`. Also include a truncated/streaming example to illustrate fallback.
Jake L: I'll add the TS/Node snippet and update the samples index to point to both snippets + migration guide.
Olivia P: Also rename flag instances: `compact_response` -> `compact_mode` (we changed the API flag last week). I'll do a search-and-replace in docs.
docs-bot: Note: docs PR #4821 references `compact-response` and will conflict.
Samir: Owners: Maria (Python + migration note), Jake (TS + index update), Olivia (links + flag rename), Samir (write parse-fallback paragraph + envelope example). Target: EOD tomorrow for thin PRs.
Maria Chen: I'll include an eval snippet for monitoring parse failures: `parse_fail_rate = failed_parses / total_calls` under "how to monitor".
Jake L: For raw shape examples, I'll show `raw` as a string and note `json.loads(raw)` for structured raw payloads.
Olivia P: Queueing linkfix PR now, tagging @docs-owners. :thumbsup:
Samir: After PRs land, I'll collate a short release-note blurb. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
